rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two things already in the archive — the maturity-rank conditioner from "Maturity-Weighted Financing Discretion" (alpha 0.042, t=3.82) and the positive/negative-part asymmetry template already applied in "Debt-Use Issuance Attenuation" and "Revenue-Absorption Issuance Test" — so it is a cosmetic decomposition rather than a new mechanism, and by construction it can only shrink the archived signal's conditioning.

The exact mirror of the preceding proposal (their weighted parts sum back to the archived maturity-weighted signal), it is again a cosmetic asymmetric split of an existing best performer, and its economic story is weaker — low current debt as a marker of "discretionary" issuance conflicts with the more standard reading that distressed, high-short-debt issuers are the ones that underperform.

Replacing gross dlc/at with uncovered current debt max(dlc−che,0)/at is a genuine and economically better-motivated change to the conditioning state of the archive's strongest mechanism, though the positive-part construction leaves a large mass of firms at exactly zero, so IND_RANK will produce a coarse, tie-heavy conditioner that may blunt rather than sharpen the archived result.

Pairing the liquidity-capped repurchase leg with a distinct structural-solvency rank is a defensible non-redundant extension of an archived signal, but multiplying the whole financing z-score by NEG(lt/at) rank also attenuates the issuance short leg precisely for high-leverage issuers — the group most likely to underperform — which works against the hypothesis and risks weakening the alpha it aims to improve.

The construction is internally incoherent: the archived organic-book leg worked because Δceq mechanically contains net equity issuance (a clean accounting identity), whereas Δsale does not, so subtracting issuance dollars from a revenue change is an arbitrary mixing of incommensurable quantities that mostly reduces to a value tilt plus the well-known net-share-issuance anomaly.

The expression faithfully implements the stated hypothesis and the organic-book gate is a legitimate accounting-identity-based validation of buybacks, but it is a fairly predictable splice of two archived constructs (the organic-book leg and the gated-gross-repurchase-minus-sstk template), so incremental information over those is likely modest.
